gap: No result ChatGPT got states a side-by-side of named measurements across the 20,000 mAh, 100 W-class candidates: only the UGREEN Nexode 130W has load-by-load delivered energy (Best Batteries, 54.8 to 64.7 Wh), while Macworld's recharge scores and Notebookcheck's meter reading cover the Anker Prime 220W and Cuktech 15 Ultra, and no named reviewer has measured the Baseus FC41 20K 100W or UGREEN 20K 100W.
standout_why: Compared against us.best-batteries.com/reviews/ugreen-nexode-20000-130w (rank 8, not cited), its /power-banks/ twin, Macworld's UGREEN 130W review (cited), MacSources and Parka Blogs. Best Batteries already gives the strongest measurement for the pick: 54.8 to 64.7 Wh delivered of 72 Wh, 100 W falling to 65 W after about 22 minutes, and 'about 1.1 of a 13-inch MacBook Air'. Macworld's review already has 56% of an Air M3 in 30 minutes. What those pages lack is any other candidate's measurements beside it, and the 15-inch Air arithmetic against Apple's 66.5 Wh. The new part is thin and uneven: Macworld's scores use a 14-inch MacBook Pro, not an Air, and none covers the 130W UGREEN.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20K 130W rather than changing the pick: it is the only candidate whose delivered energy was measured at laptop loads (57.9 Wh at 60 W), and that is about 1.08 times Apple's 53.8 Wh 13-inch Air battery but only 0.87 of the 66.5 Wh 15-inch. So the page can say 'one full 13-inch charge, not a full 15-inch charge' with a name on it. The Baseus FC41 20K 100W and UGREEN 20K 100W can only be ranked on maker figures. Two cautions for the writer: the '13-inch Air with about 5% remaining' line in Macworld's roundup sits in a Baseus 100W 20K entry (74 Wh), not a UGREEN one, and reads as a capacity statement rather than a logged test; and Macworld's 123% for the Cuktech 15 Ultra should not be used as a capacity ranking (see note).

findings.label: Delivered energy by load (Best Batteries, Guillaume Hoarau)
findings.value: 62.4 Wh at 5 V/2 A; 63.4 Wh at 9 V/1 A; 64.7 Wh at 9 V/3 A; 61.0 Wh at 20 V/1 A; 57.9 Wh at 20 V/3 A (60 W); 54.8 Wh at 20 V/5 A (100 W); 76 to 90% of the 72 Wh claimed
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Review published 2026-10-09. Method as described on the page: constant electronic load plus two real laptops; no instrument named. This page was already in ChatGPT's results (rank 8), so it is not new to the answer.

findings.label: How long the 100 W port holds 100 W (Best Batteries, Guillaume Hoarau)
findings.value: On constant load, 100 W falls to 65 W after about 22 min with 34% left; with real laptops it fell to 45 W after 18 min with 50% left
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Review published 2026-10-09. Relevant to the Air because Apple's fast-charge line is 70 W: the step-down to 65 W or 45 W puts the port below it for the second half of the charge.

findings.label: MacBook Air M3 charge gained in 30 minutes (Macworld, Thomas Bergbold)
findings.value: 56% in 30 min from USB-C1; iPhone 15 55%, 11-inch iPad Pro 36% in the same time
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Review dated 2024-09-07. Air size (13 or 15 inch) and measured watts are not given. Already cited by ChatGPT.

findings.label: Recharge input and time, three named readings
findings.value: Macworld (Bergbold): no more than 70 W, full in under 2 hours. MacSources (Jon Walters): 20.19 V/3.14 A on a multimeter (about 63.4 W), bank display 60.9 W, 12% to 49% in 29 min. Best Batteries (Hoarau): starts at about 62 W, falls to 25 to 45 W after 10 to 30 min, full in 1 h 45 to 2 h 40
findings.source_title: UGREEN 130W Nexode 20000 Power Bank 2024 REVIEW - MacSources
findings.note: MacSources dated 2024-09-11, charged from a UGREEN 160W Nexode Pro brick, Klein Tools multimeter; 20.19 x 3.14 = 63.4 W is my arithmetic. The Macworld and Best Batteries figures are from the two URLs in the findings above, read the same day.

findings.label: Weight as weighed by reviewers
findings.value: Macworld lists 16.9 oz (480 g); MacSources weighed 1 lb 0.6 oz (about 471 g) and quotes 476 g as the stated weight
findings.source_title: UGREEN 130W Nexode 20000 Power Bank 2024 REVIEW - MacSources
findings.note: 16.6 oz x 28.35 = 470.6 g is my arithmetic. MacSources also saw 84.4 W on the bank's display into a 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro (multimeter 19.93 V/3.39 A).

findings.label: MacBook Air battery sizes and fast-charge threshold (Apple)
findings.value: 13-inch: 53.8 Wh; 15-inch: 66.5 Wh; both M5; 'Fast-charge capable with 70W or higher USB PD power source'
findings.note: Current US spec page. The in-box adapter is listed as a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W max.

findings.label: Arithmetic: Best Batteries' delivered energy against Apple's Air batteries
findings.value: At 60 W (57.9 Wh): 1.08 x a 13-inch Air, 0.87 x a 15-inch Air. At 100 W (54.8 Wh): 1.02 x 13-inch, 0.82 x 15-inch
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: My division: 57.9/53.8, 57.9/66.5, 54.8/53.8, 54.8/66.5, using Apple's Wh figures from apple.com/macbook-air/specs. These are ceilings: the Mac's own charging losses are not subtracted and nobody measured them. Best Batteries itself says 'about 1.1 of a 13-inch MacBook Air' and 'charges once, barely'; the 15-inch figure is the part I did not see on its page.
